title: Duodenal Mucosa Responses to Endoscopic Food Challenges in Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Self-reported Food Intolerances: A Feasibility Study
official: Duodenal Responses to Food Challenges in Patients With Self-reported Food Intolerances: a Feasibility Study
summary:
The goal of this study is to investigate the feasibility of using intravenous fluorescein during a standard endoscopy-along with a laser to activate it and an optical filter-to identify changes in the duodenal mucosa after a controlled food challenge in individuals with IBD and IBS who experience food intolerances. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is this technique feasible approach to assess food intolerances in patients with IBD and IBS?
* Does patients with IBD and IBS exhibit acute tissue changes upon exposure to specific food antigens?

Researches will compare the food antigen to a placebo solution (saline solution without an antigen) to see if the reaction in the tissue is different.

Participants will:

* Answer questionnaires.
* Provide a blood and stool sample.
* Take an allergy test.
* Undergo an upper endoscopy.

interventions.name: Upper diagnostic endoscopy with food challenges and biopsies

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Confirmed diagnosis of IBD (UC or CD) and under clinical remission for at least 3 months, OR confirmed diagnosis of IBS (any subtype) by Rome IV criteria.
* Report having one or more food intolerance.
* Able to provide informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of a known food allergy.
* Presence of serum IgE positivity or a positive skin-prick test to cow's milk.
* Known allergy to fluorescein.
* Diagnosis of celiac disease.
* Positive IgA TTG antibodies.
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
* Presence of a contraindication for an upper endoscopy.
* History of surgery involving the upper gastrointestinal tract.
